title: ר' יהודה בן בתירא

paragraphs: (a) In the Mishnah: Peah 3:6; Bikkurim 1:6; Shabbat 9:7; Pesachim 3:3; Yevamot 4:9; Ketubot 6:1; Nedarim 6:8; Gittin 2:4; Shevuot 3:6; Eduyot 8:3; Arakhin 8:6; Kelim 2:4; Ohalot 11:7; Negaim 9:3, Negaim 11:7; Mikvaot 4:5.

(b) He is the unqualified ben Beteira; see there. Sometimes the unqualified R. Yehudah is R. Yehudah ben Beteira; see R. Yehudah bar Ilai. Yuchasin, in the sequence of generations after Admon and Chanan, writes that the sons of Beteira were in Shemayah and Avtalyon's group, like Akavya, since Hillel was nasi after them. Rashi, Taanit, chapter 1, says the sons of Beteira in Hillel's time were R. Yehudah ben Beteira and his brother R. Yehoshua; Shalshelet HaKabbalah, 27, adds Shimon, and says they descended from Jesse and were academy heads at Jerusalem. This is not clear, since Jerusalem Talmud, end of Arba Mitot, says R. Yehudah ben Beteira was born through R. Eliezer's and R. Yehoshua's prayer, and R. Yehoshua was Hillel's student. Its words: once R. Eliezer, R. Yehoshua, and Rabban Gamliel went to Rome. They came to a Jew's home. For every dish he brought, he first entered a room and then brought it before them. They asked why. He answered that his elderly father had vowed not to leave the room until he saw Israel's sages. They told him to ask his father to come. When he came, they asked his concern. He said, “Pray for my son, who has no children.” R. Eliezer told R. Yehoshua, “See what you will do,” suspecting that he had been bewitched, and R. Yehoshua was expert in sorcery. R. Yehoshua ordered flaxseed brought, sowed it on a board, and it began growing. As he began pulling it out, he drew out a woman by her hair and told her to undo her sorcery. She refused. He threatened to expose her if she refused. She said she could not, since she had cast it into the sea. R. Yehoshua decreed upon the sea's prince, and it was expelled. He prayed, and the man merited fathering R. Yehudah ben Beteira. They said, “Had we come here only to bring forth this righteous man, it would suffice.” How, then, could the sons of Beteira who relinquished the presidency because they did not know one law, and were replaced by Hillel (see there), be R. Yehudah ben Beteira, who was born through the prayer of R. Yehoshua, Hillel's student? End of chapter 9 of Negaim: he presented arguments before R. Eliezer, who told him, “You are a great sage”; likewise 11:7. Ketubot 14a: he testified with R. Yehoshua; this requires investigation. Lechem Shamayim, Peah, chapter 3, writes that the sons of Beteira who yielded the presidency to Hillel were not those in the mishnayot. R. Yehudah ben Beteira was their son or grandson. Hence they are called “the sons of Beteira” there, and Hillel did not call them by name. Taanit, chapter 1, answers that before ordination they were called sons of Beteira, but this cannot be, since they were presidents; see there. R. Yehudah ben Beteira was in Babylonia at Nisibis in the Temple period, as in Pesachim 3b: a Cuthean told him he ate the Passover sacrifices. R. Yehudah ben Beteira asked whether they had given him the fat tail, etc. They told him, “You are at Nisibis, yet your net is spread in Jerusalem.” Rashbam explains that he did not make the pilgrimage because he was old and exempt from appearance, or owned no land. Nisibis is thus outside the Land. See immediately below: Sifrei, Reeh, likewise proves it is outside the Land; Lechem Shamayim says in Assyria. The region of Nisibis is near Assyria; in the city of Netziv is R. Yehudah ben Beteira's synagogue: Gelilot Eretz Yisrael; see Ezra the scribe. “Follow R. Yehudah ben Beteira to Nisibis”—Sanhedrin 32b. He lived many years until Rav's and Shmuel's time, since Shmuel was born through R. Yehudah ben Beteira's blessing to Abba, his father; see there. Shabbat, R. Eliezer, 130a, and Kol HaBasar, Chullin 113, 116a, apparently place him also in Levi's time. Levi told Rabbi it was R. Yehudah ben Beteira's locality and supposed that ben Beteira had taught them according to R. Yosi HaGelili. Chullin 54a: Yosef the bird-catcher asked R. Yehudah ben Beteira. We find Levi with Yosef the bird-catcher. Rambam writes R. Yehudah ben Beteira belonged to Hillel's and Shammai's group and did not see the destruction. Dorot Olam says he lived after the destruction, in the time of the ten martyrs, Ben Azzai, Ben Zoma, R. Chutzpit, and R. Akiva, and was at Nisibis. His colleague was Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai. Beginning of Yom Tov, Rosh Hashanah, chapter 4, 29b: after the Temple's destruction, Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai instituted that the horn be sounded on the Sabbath wherever there was a court. Once Rosh Hashanah fell on the Sabbath. Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai told the sons of Beteira, “Let us sound”; they answered, “Let us discuss, etc.” He lived long after the destruction: Sifrei, Reeh, on “When He cuts off,” says R. Elazar ben Shamua and R. Yochanan the sandal-maker went to Nisibis to learn from R. Yehudah ben Beteira. At Sidon they remembered the Land of Israel, wept, and returned. Likewise at the end of Ketubot. R. Yochanan the sandal-maker and R. Elazar ben Shamua, R. Akiva's students, were the third generation after the destruction. Sifrei there says R. Yehudah ben Beteira, R. Matya ben Cheresh, and R. Chananyah, son of R. Yehoshua's brother, tore their clothes when leaving the Land; see there. R. Yehudah ben Beteira requires investigation, since he lived at Nisibis outside the Land. Yevamot, chapter 12, 102a: R. Yosi said, “When I went to Nisibis, I found an elder and asked if he knew R. Yehudah ben Beteira. He said, ‘Yes; he is regularly at my table.’” Tosafot on the Jerusalem Talmud, cited by Asheri there, reads, “I was a money-changer in my town, and he was always at my table.” R. Yosi likewise belonged to that third group, as R. Akiva's student. Yevamot, Beit Shammai, 108b: they asked R. Akiva in prison and he forbade; they asked R. Yehudah ben Beteira at Nisibis and he forbade. Shabbat 96b, 97a: R. Yehudah ben Beteira told Akiva, “Either way, you will be called to account.” Nazir 56b and Tosefta Nazir, chapter 5: R. Elazar (see there) said, “I found R. Meir and R. Yehudah ben Beteira discussing according to the law. R. Yehudah says a quarter-log of blood does not require a nazirite to shave. R. Meir told him, etc. Ben Beteira was silent. I told R. Meir, ‘Do you know Yehoshua ben Mammal?’ He answered, ‘Yes, he is a master of laws.’” This is long after the destruction, since R. Meir was third-generation, R. Akiva's student, and eventually went down to Babylonia when his wife died. Beer Sheva, Chelek, Sanhedrin 96a, discusses R. Zeira saying: “Although R. Yehudah ben Beteira sent from Nisibis: take care concerning an elder who forgot his learning through circumstances beyond his control; take care concerning the veins according to R. Yehudah; take care concerning the children of the unlearned, from whom Torah will emerge, etc.” He writes that this never happened, since R. Yehudah ben Beteira lived long before the unqualified R. Yehudah of the Mishnah at the beginning of HaShochet, “R. Yehudah says: until he slaughters the veins,” namely R. Yehudah bar Ilai. R. Yehudah ben Beteira was with Shammai and Hillel before the Second Temple's destruction; R. Yehudah was with R. Meir and R. Yosi, the third group after the destruction, etc. It must therefore read “R. Yehoshua ben Levi said: take care concerning the veins according to R. Yehudah.” So too Berakhot, chapter 1, 8b: R. Yehoshua ben Levi told his sons, “Complete your portions with the congregation, twice Scripture and once translation; take care concerning the veins according to R. Yehudah; take care concerning an elder who forgot his learning through circumstances beyond his control.” End of quotation. Incidentally, see Arukh, entry Veridin: Chullin, chapter 2, 27, R. Yehudah says to slaughter the veins. It also cites Berakhot, Tefillat HaShachar, 28, R. Nechunya ben HaKanah, and Chelek there, “Take care concerning the veins according to R. Yehudah.” End of quotation. This is an error: nothing of this appears in Tefillat HaShachar, only in chapter 1, 8b, above. Beer Sheva thus deleted R. Yehudah ben Beteira in Chelek and emended to R. Yehoshua ben Levi because of the difficulty that ben Beteira lived in Hillel's time and R. Yehudah in R. Meir's third-generation group. How did he forget Tosafot, Menachot 65b: “R. Yehudah ben Beteira says, etc.; above R. Yehudah ben Beteira expounds otherwise. In Rabbenu Gershom's book ben Beteira is deleted, leaving the unqualified R. Yehudah. Perhaps there were two: one lived in the Temple period, as Pesachim 3b proves, and another is the one whose father's sorcery R. Eliezer and R. Yehoshua annulled, as the Jerusalem Talmud relates.” Thus according to Tosafot there is no need to delete ben Beteira: the ben Beteira who ruled like R. Yehudah concerning the veins was the second. It appears even more necessary that there were two: the sons of Beteira presided before Hillel, whose presidency began one hundred years before the destruction. Presumably they were no younger than thirty or forty when appointed and also presided some years before yielding to Hillel; thus they were about 150 years before the destruction. R. Yehudah ben Beteira is found in Levi's and Shmuel's time, Rabbi's students, at least one hundred years after the destruction. He would therefore be 250 years old. Necessarily there were two—or necessarily one who lived exceptionally long. In any case, R. Yehudah ben Beteira lived in R. Meir's time and that of the students R. Yosi and R. Yehudah bar Ilai. Beer Sheva's difficulty falls away; he deleted ben Beteira in Chelek needlessly. A thousand pardons to his holy remains: given his great learning, known from his books, how did all this escape him?

(c) Ramban, Torat HaAdam, is uncertain whether R. Yehudah ben Beteira is R. Yehudah ben Teima, because they said one thing. Chagigah, chapter 2, 14a, says of him: “Support and staff”—these are masters of Mishnah, such as R. Yehudah ben Beteira; this is Ein Yaakov's reading. Another version, our version, has: “Staff: R. Yehudah ben Teima and his colleagues,” who knew six hundred orders of Mishnah from Moses to Hillel. Perhaps this caused Ramban's uncertainty. It is no proof, since the Jerusalem Talmud sometimes chooses a tanna whom the Babylonian Talmud did not choose; see the general rules.

(d) They descend from the presidents at Jerusalem before Hillel, and are descendants of those dead whom Ezekiel revived. He said, “These phylacteries are from them”: Chelek, Sanhedrin 92b. Benjamin's Travels writes that he is buried at Meron; see R. Shimon ben Yochai.

(e) In R. Elazar ben Matya's name. R. Elazar, in his name: Tosefta Ohalot, chapter 12. Elazar ben Pinchas, in his name. He said to R. Eliezer: end of chapter 9 of Negaim. Ben Bag Bag sent to him. R. Yoshiyah said, “I spoke to R. Yehudah ben Beteira”; see there. He testified with R. Yehoshua: Ketubot 14a; compare Menachot 103b, where the witness is named R. Yehoshua ben Beteira. R. Yochanan, in his name: Avodah Zarah, chapter 2, 30b, near the end.
